counterexamples.evidence: All three handles appear in the assembled prompt under ‘# You MUST build the explanation around these’, yet runs 1 and 2 emitted no [zone:] tag at all (checked on row.raw, pre-processAnnotations); the served prose therefore promises ‘your four-in-a-row line’ and ‘the decisive squares’ with nothing highlightable behind them. Enforcement of the required set is not part of the harness single-call path, so the omission reaches the served string.

Run 1 places ‘the decisive squares in the lower-middle’. visualize_board.sh on render_decision.finalMovestring shows the winning group is the horizontal c2r5,c3r5,c4r5,c5r5 completed by Green at c5r5 on move 41 — row 5 of 6, not the lower middle. The prompt never uses any region wording.

Runs 1 and 2 name only the two move columns (3 and 4); no cell or window from the offered alias set survives into the prose, so the parity idea has no square instantiating it for the player who just blundered.
